_comment: Descriptor of the rev A Hall-effect coupon (default slot S1, standard), written from its captured design (keyboard/hardware/design/sheets/coupon_hall.py, DESCRIPTOR_FACTS and the parts notes; captured 2026-11-27, re-captured 2026-11-28 for the owner's decisions of 2026-11-27) and its netlist. Not built: the currents are the design's estimates and the scaling is the datasheet's typical sensitivity (placeholder_fields). tests/test_rules.py compares it with DESCRIPTOR_FACTS.
notes: Lanes: AN0 = U10 TMUX1208 8:1 mux -> U12A OPA2365 follower -> R18 22 ohm (sites SEL 0-7: K1-K4, REF1, REF2, TEMP1, TEMP2); AN1 = K1 (U20) direct -> U12B follower -> R19 22 ohm. R_src 23 ohm: the 22 ohm plus the follower's closed-loop output impedance (< 1 ohm at DC by the design's estimate), rounded up

AN2 is open as assembled: R26 (0 ohm, DNP) would put the mux output on it unbuffered (the SPEC §11 #21 experiment); fitting R26 needs a new descriptor (AN2 in uses, R_src = TMAG5253 1.27 ohm + TMUX1208 RON 9 typ / 15 max, CLoad 1 nF). AN3 is not connected
CLoad 1000 pF: the OPA2365 is 'stable with a pure capacitive load up to approximately 1 nF' at unity gain (SBOS365G §8.3.3, the design's reading); the 22 ohm isolates the lane's 1 nF

Scaling: TMAG5253BA4 7.5 mV/mT at 3.3 V, VQ = VCC/2 (sheets/coupon_hall.py from SBASAI5E): B = (ratio - 0.5) x 3300 / 7.5 = (ratio - 0.5) x 440 mT, a typical figure, not calibrated. Steps 6 and 7 of AN0 are the thermistor taps (ext.sites), which the driver converts itself

+3V3: the design's estimate is 25 mA typ all-on (6 x 2.6 mA sensors + 9.2 mA buffers + 0.33 mA thermistors), 41 mA max; max_ma 45 adds the descriptor EEPROM's read current and rounds up. +5V is not used
Bulk on +3V3 at the header: C1 10 uF + ten 100 nF = 11 uF (the netlist)

G-lines: G0-G2 = SEL[2:0] (mux A0-A2 and latch S0-S2), G3 = SEL_EN (mux EN and latch D), G4 = latch G (active low), G5 = latch CLR (active low); every G-line has a 100 k pull-down on the coupon. Modes in sheets/coupon_hall.py DESCRIPTOR_FACTS['modes']. G4/G5 are slow expander lines on S1-S4: fine, they only set the mode
needs lanes_14bit: AN1 is a 14-bit key lane; on S5 it would land on the 12-bit ADC4 (SPEC §4.4)
devices[3] is the SN74HC259 enable latch (U11): format 1.0 has no part ID for it, so 'other' on bus gpio
Pin 39 is the slot key (owner's decision D2 of 2026-11-27): no pin, no pad, no net on this coupon; it is in no `uses` group. Stage A1 (D1)

Crosstalk (risks.md SE-2, the register's field model, an estimate): a press to the 4 mm stop moves REF1 by -205 uT for K1 or K3 and -8 uT for K2 or K4 (REF2 the mirror image), a key's row or column neighbour by -137 uT and its diagonal by -28 uT, against a sensor's 25.8 uT rms. A reference is common mode only while every key reads at rest; otherwise subtract the 4 x 6 matrix measured at bring-up (DESCRIPTOR_FACTS['crosstalk_uT'])

Electronic floor (risks.md SE-4): AN0 steps 6 and 7 (TEMP1, TEMP2, the thermistor taps behind 1 uF) pass the same mux, U12A, R18 and lane as the sensors, every frame, near mid-scale; their own noise is about 9 uV rms (estimate) against the ADC's 233-464 uV rms, so their sigma is the lane's floor. AN1 has no floor source of its own (with K1 off, R20 holds it at 0 V): use AN0's

devices.note: U20-U25: K1-K4, REF1, REF2; K1 also on AN1
U11 SN74HC259 enable latch on G0-G5
